crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The algorithms are fixed by the specifications: BIP32 fixes HMAC-SHA512 and secp256k1, and the scripts a descriptor expands to fix hash160, SHA-256 and BIP340 keys, as Bitcoin's consensus rules do. A user cannot switch to another without leaving the format; another algorithm needs a soft fork and a new BIP first. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/README.md#what-is-here
crypto_call_justification: The package reimplements no primitive. BIP32's HMAC-SHA512 is the standard library's hmac; hash160 and RIPEMD-160 are btclib's; the curve arithmetic, BIP340's tagged hash and MuSig2 key aggregation are ecc's, which reaches libsecp256k1 through btclib-secp256k1 where the secp256k1 extra is installed. What the package writes itself is what the BIPs define above them: BIP32's derivation steps, the descriptor checksum and the miniscript compiler. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/tree/main/src/bip32_descriptors
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: bip32-descriptors performs no network communications, so it uses no TLS: no module under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/tree/main/src/bip32_descriptors
crypto_credential_agility_justification: bip32-descriptors is a library with no configuration file, credential store or password: it derives and parses the keys and descriptors a caller passes in, and keeps nothing. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#threat-model
crypto_floss_justification: No closed-source dependency: base58-bech32, btclib, ecc and typing-extensions, and with the secp256k1 extra btclib-secp256k1, the libsecp256k1 it builds from, cffi and pycparser, are all FLOSS. This tree imports nothing else outside the standard library. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/pyproject.toml
crypto_keylength_justification: Keys are secp256k1 keys, about 128 bits of security, above NIST's 112-bit minimum for 2030. rootxprv_from_seed refuses a seed under 128 or over 512 bits, the range BIP32 sets. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/src/bip32_descriptors/bip32/bip32.py
crypto_password_storage_justification: The package stores no password and authenticates no one: it has no user, account or secret of its own.
crypto_pfs_justification: The package implements no network key-agreement protocol: it performs no network communications at all.
crypto_published_justification: Every algorithm is a published one: HMAC-SHA512 (RFC 2104, FIPS 180-4) and secp256k1 (SEC 2) in BIP32, hash160 (SHA-256 then RIPEMD-160) for fingerprints and scripts, and BIP340's tagged hashes and BIP327's MuSig2 key aggregation for taproot descriptors. BIP380's descriptor checksum is a BCH code that detects errors and is not cryptography. Each is checked against the vectors its authors publish. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/README.md#what-is-here
crypto_random_justification: The package draws no random number: nothing under src/ imports random or secrets or reads os.urandom. A seed is the caller's. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/tree/main/src/bip32_descriptors
crypto_tls12_justification: bip32-descriptors performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/tree/main/src/bip32_descriptors
crypto_used_network_justification: bip32-descriptors does not use the network: no module under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib, and ASSURANCE_CASE.md's threat model states it opens no socket. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/tree/main/src/bip32_descriptors
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: bip32-descriptors performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/tree/main/src/bip32_descriptors
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or MD5 appears under src/. BIP32's HMAC-SHA512 comes from hmac in bip32.py. RIPEMD-160 appears only where Bitcoin fixes it: inside hash160, for BIP32's fingerprints and the script templates; in descriptors.py's direct call to btclib's ripemd160, which turns a P2WSH program into the hash160 of its script to look the script up; and in miniscript's ripemd160() hashlock, which BIP379 defines and which commits with OP_RIPEMD160. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/tree/main/src/bip32_descriptors
crypto_working_justification: No broken cryptographic algorithm: HMAC-SHA512, SHA-256, RIPEMD-160 inside hash160, and secp256k1, as BIP32 and Bitcoin fix them.

dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No vulnerability found by dynamic analysis is known or open: the scheduled fuzz run of 2026-11-03 reported no crash (https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/actions/runs/41636358585). Issue #19 reported inputs of a seeded fuzz run that parse and Bitcoin Core both refuse with different faults, filed as a defect and not as a vulnerability; pull requests 29 and 117 fixed it, and it was closed on 2026-11-07. #6, an input of Core's qa-assets corpus that parse accepted and Core refuses, was fixed by pull request 31 on 2026-11-01. The scheduled mutation run of 2026-11-02 passed with survivors, 210 in descriptors and 51 in bip32 (https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/actions/runs/41456861722). A survivor is a mutant the tests did not catch, a test gap and not itself a vulnerability. The 333 survivors of the 2026-10-31 run were triaged on 2026-11-01: none revealed a code bug on the inputs measured; the gaps on security-relevant checks, issues #32 to #40, are closed, and #41, the ordinary ones, is open. No issue records a triage of the 2026-11-02 run's survivors. The evidence is partial: that run judged 688 of 14026 descriptors mutants and 835 of 1610 bip32 mutants.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Every release runs the test suite and the regtest tests before it is published: release.yml calls test.yml and integration-bitcoind.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if both pass, as they did for v2026.11.13 (https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/actions/runs/43332607429). The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. fuzz.yml runs two ClusterFuzzLite atheris harnesses weekly, fuzz/fuzz_bip32.py over the BIP32 wire decoders and fuzz/fuzz_descriptor.py over descriptor parsing; its scheduled run of 2026-11-03 ran each for 30 minutes with no reportable crash (https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/actions/runs/41636358585). mutation.yml runs cosmic-ray weekly on .github/mutation/bip32.toml and on the shards of the descriptors profile under .github/mutation/. Its time-budgeted scheduled run of 2026-11-02 executed part of each profile: bip32 killed 784, survived 51, skipped 242, never run 533; descriptors killed 478, survived 210, never run 13338 (https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/actions/runs/41456861722). qa-assets.yml replays Bitcoin Core's descriptor fuzz corpus weekly; its scheduled run of 2026-11-03 passed (https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/actions/runs/41627321869). https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml

hardened_site_justification: The download site, PyPI's project page, sends no Content-Security-Policy, and that header is PyPI's to set. Measured with curl -sIL on 2026-11-14: the project page https://btclib.org/bip32-descriptors/ sends Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options DENY and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and the repository and its releases page on github.com send all four. PyPI's project page https://pypi.org/project/bip32-descriptors/ sends Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options deny and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and no Content-Security-Policy. The documentation site https://bip32-descriptors.readthedocs.io/, which the criterion does not name, sends Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and neither Content-Security-Policy nor X-Frame-Options.
hardening_justification: The shipped package keeps private key material out of repr. BIP32KeyData.__repr__, in src/bip32_descriptors/bip32/bip32.py, prints *** for the key and the chain code of a private key, and _BIP32KeyData, the mutable copy derivation works on, is declared @dataclass(repr=False) in the same file, so its repr prints no field. A defect that puts one of these objects in a log line or an exception message, through its repr or str, therefore shows no private key. ruff's bandit S rules and CodeQL find defects before a release, which is not hardening, and the package is pure Python, so no compiler flag applies. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/src/bip32_descriptors/bip32/bip32.py
implement_secure_design_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* applies Saltzer and Schroeder's principles one by one: economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, open design, least privilege and psychological acceptability, each to the parser, check or test that carries it. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#secure-design-principles
input_validation_justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid with btclib's BTClibTypeError or BTClibValueError, or ecc's class of the same kind where an argument reaches that package, as CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* requires. tests/input_validation_test.py drives the rule over every public function, and tests/fuzz_test.py holds every parser to it on hostile input. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-public-surface
installation_common_justification: `python -m pip install --upgrade bip32-descriptors` installs it from PyPI, as README.md says, and pypi-install.yml installs the published version on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows after each release and weekly. https://pypi.org/project/bip32-descriptors/
installation_development_quick_justifica: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command, uv being the only tool to install first; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates

internationalization_justification: The package produces no text for end users and sorts none: it turns keys, paths and descriptors into scripts, addresses and their ASCII spellings, and its exceptions are English messages for developers. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/tree/main/src/bip32_descriptors

maintained_justification: The repository opened on 2026-10-31 with the BIP32, descriptor and miniscript code started from btclib-wallet 910ba96, a local integration of the pull requests for btclib-wallet issue #620 before they landed (the last, #631, as 78e360b); its src/btclib_wallet/bip32 and src/btclib_wallet/descriptors equal those of 1fa1a78, #631's first commit. Six releases followed, v2026.11.2, v2026.11.4, v2026.11.7, v2026.11.11, v2026.11.12 and v2026.11.13, and main has opened the next cycle, 2026.12. Counted on 2026-11-13 with `gh release list -R btclib-org/bip32-descriptors --exclude-drafts --json tagName,publishedAt -q '[.[] | select(.publishedAt > "2026-10-31T17:10:01Z") | .tagName]'`, which prints the releases published after v2026.10.31. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/commits/main https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/releases
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*). release.yml compares each release's public API with the previous tag's using griffe; v2026.10.31 was the first release, and the comparison passed for v2026.11.13 against v2026.11.12 (https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/actions/runs/43332607429). RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: detect-secrets baseline gated by pre-commit, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection enabled on the repository: https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
osps_ac_02_01_justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor, fametrano, holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the approval but still refuses a direct push, so nobody pushes to main directly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. An administrator's merge bypasses the lint check: enforce_admins is off. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. The mention job holds a secret on any pull request's issue comment, and there checks out the default branch. It answers only a comment whose author is an owner, a member or a collaborator, and its tools exclude Bash, edits, writes, file reads and every tool Claude Code marked as running code when last measured, on 2.1.301. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: A workflow_dispatch input is either mutation.yml's profile, a choice from the fixed list its `options:` holds, or verified-signatures.yml's before and after, which the called workflow reads through env: and refuses unless they are commit shas. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D, or YYYY.M.D.N for a patch), declared in pyproject.toml and matched by a signed v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/releases
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name, as v2026.11.13's do: the sdist (bip32_descriptors-2026.11.13.tar.gz), the wheel (bip32_descriptors-2026.11.13-py3-none-any.whl), the CycloneDX SBOM (bip32_descriptors-2026.11.13.cdx.json) and the attestation bundle (v2026.11.13.intoto.jsonl). The attestation binds each asset to its digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/releases/tag/v2026.11.13
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://bip32-descriptors.readthedocs.io/.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/bip32-descriptors/
osps_br_04_01_justification: The GitHub release body is RELEASE_NOTES.md's entry: what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. CHANGELOG.md lists every change. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. The GitHub release carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle over each asset's SHA-256. The tag is signed. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/releases/latest
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. An administrator's merge bypasses the lint check: enforce_admins is off. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_br_07_02_justification: A secret is an environment secret that only the owners reach. A secret kept in any other store is recorded in the REPOSITORY.md of the repository that uses it, and btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded one. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected. The secrets kept outside an environment are rotated before they are a year old, and the list is reviewed yearly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_do_01_01_justification: The user documentation is README.md, whose Python example tests/readme_test.py runs, and the API reference on Read the Docs. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/README.md#a-key-a-descriptor-an-address https://bip32-descriptors.readthedocs.io/
osps_do_02_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml
osps_do_03_01_justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist and the wheel from their tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_03_02_justification: The verify command pins the signer and the source: --owner btclib-org, --signer-workflow the organization's reusable-build.yml and --source-ref the release tag, and it compares the certificate's sourceRepositoryIdentifier with this repository's id, which a rename keeps. osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_06_01_justification: pyproject.toml says beside each runtime dependency (base58-bech32, btclib, ecc and typing-extensions) and beside the secp256k1 extra (ecc[secp256k1], which brings btclib-secp256k1) why it is one, and CONTRIBUTING.md's *The one constraint* says what the package imports. uv obtains every dependency from PyPI and pins it in uv.lock, and Dependabot tracks them weekly with a seven-day cooldown. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/pyproject.toml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci
osps_do_07_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
osps_gv_01_01_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, names who holds access to sensitive resources. fametrano is the maintainer. Every owner, named there by login, is an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_01_02_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, describes the maintainer, owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: A grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_le_01_01_justification: The criterion's details say a platform such as GitHub may include the assertion in its terms of service, and GitHub's do: section D.6 says that whoever adds content to a repository with a licence agrees that they have the right to license it under those terms. main also requires the lint / Sign-off check, which fails on a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer, Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s aside. Web commits are signed off automatically. An administrator's merge bypasses that check: enforce_admins is off. https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service#6-contributions-under-repository-license https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released wheel and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/bip32-descriptors/
osps_le_03_01_justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies: base58-bech32, btclib, ecc and typing-extensions at run time, the optional secp256k1 extra, and the development tools in dependency groups. The committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_02_02_justification: The release is pure Python. Every GitHub release attaches a CycloneDX SBOM generated from the built wheel and covered by the release attestation. v2026.11.13's, bip32_descriptors-2026.11.13.cdx.json, lists base58-bech32, btclib, ecc and typing-extensions as required. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/releases/tag/v2026.11.13
osps_qa_03_01_justification: main requires six status checks: test: every job passed, docs / Build the documentation, lint / Lint and type-check, lint / Dependency review, lint / Sign-off and regtest / Regtest against Bitcoin Core. enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without the checks is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The project has no subproject: each release is built from this one repository, as pyproject.toml shows. base58-bech32, btclib, ecc and btclib-secp256k1, which it depends on, are separate projects with their own repositories. The organization standard's section 2 lists btclib-org's repositories and their tiers, bip32-descriptors at tier 1. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far
osps_qa_04_02_justification: The project has no additional subproject repository: each release is built from this one repository. base58-bech32, btclib, ecc and btclib-secp256k1, which it depends on, are released separately from their own repositories, held to the same standard. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable is committed. The only files git treats as binary are the Sphinx inventory docs/source/_inventories/python.inv and two of the fuzzers' input seeds under fuzz/corpus/.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: No executable, library or compiled file is committed. The Sphinx inventory docs/source/_inventories/python.inv and the fuzz seeds under fuzz/corpus/ are data, and .clusterfuzzlite/build.sh is the only file with the executable bit, a shell script.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: A pull request that is not a draft runs the integration tests against a Bitcoin Core regtest node in the required check regtest / Regtest against Bitcoin Core, and, unless it changes only prose, the files test.yml's prose-pattern matches, the suite under coverage in the required check test: every job passed. enforce_admins is off: an administrator's merge waits for no required check, so a commit can be accepted before any test suite has run on it. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/.github/workflows/integration-bitcoind.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite, and tests/README.md the integration tests' switches. CONTRIBUTING.md's *What gates a merge, and what only reports* lists the workflows that run them on pull requests, on main and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#what-gates-a-merge-and-what-only-reports
osps_qa_06_03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* states the policy: new or changed functionality must come with tests of its own, added or updated in the same pull request, and a fix must come with a test that fails without the fix. It applies to every change of functionality, major or not. The 100% line and branch coverage gate beside it fails a pull request that leaves a statement or a branch no test reaches. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author before a merge to main, and dismisses an approval on a new push. Its bypass list holds one actor, fametrano, in pull_request mode, at rest: the organization-wide bypass the maintainer kept on 2026-11-04 (btclib-org/.github#2021 and btclib-org/.github#2040). Read with gh api repos/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/rulesets/26279909 --jq '{name, bypass: [.bypass_actors[] | {actor_id, bypass_mode}], reviews: (.rules[] | select(.type == "pull_request") | .parameters | {required_approving_review_count, dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push})}', with admin rights, on 2026-11-13; actor 3296421 is fametrano (gh api users/fametrano --jq .id). GOVERNANCE.md has the maintainer add that bypass back only in an emergency, and records that it stands until the backlog settles. It is used for ordinary work: over the last two releases, 18 of the 47 pull requests merged had no approval from anybody other than their author (v2026.11.13 6 of 13, v2026.11.12 12 of 34), and fametrano merged all 47. Counted by merge time between release publications with gh pr list -R btclib-org/bip32-descriptors -s merged -L 500 -S 'merged:2026-11-11T00:31:52Z..2026-11-13T00:08:39Z' --json mergedAt,author,reviews,mergedBy -q 'group_by(.mergedAt > "2026-11-11T23:07:10Z") | map([length, ([.[] | .author.login as $a | select(any(.reviews[]; .state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a) | not)] | length), (map(.mergedBy.login) | group_by(.) | map({(.[0]): length}) | add)])', which prints for v2026.11.12 and then v2026.11.13 the pull requests merged, those without such an approval, and who merged them. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_sa_01_01_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md gives the two subpackages, bip32 and descriptors, their layers bottom-up and what each may import, which tests/imports_test.py holds. osps_sa_02_01_justification: The API reference at https://bip32-descriptors.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from it. CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* states what is public. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-public-surface
osps_sa_03_01_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered; SECURITY.md's *Where constant time ends* records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names what is defended, the adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#threat-model
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or email, and the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org. btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, says that address reaches every organization owner. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: The refusal leaks #130, #133, #153, #324 and #342 were published as public issues, and CHANGELOG.md names the release that fixed each fixed one. A GitHub security advisory on this repository would name the release that fixes it; none has been published yet. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/security/advisories
osps_vm_04_02_justification: The CycloneDX SBOM a release attaches lists, in its vulnerabilities array, every vulnerability that the tree's .github/vex.toml judges not to affect the release, with the reason. A tree with no such judgement has no vex.toml, and its SBOM has no vulnerabilities key. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_01_justification: The standard sets the threshold: actions/dependency-review-action fails a pull request that adds or changes a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/dependency-review.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_05_02_justification: release.yml runs uv audit over everything the wheel can require: base58-bech32, btclib, ecc and typing-extensions, and through the secp256k1 extra btclib-secp256k1, cffi and pycparser. The only exemption is an id that the tree's own .github/vex.toml, carried into the release's signed SBOM, states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_03_justification: An administrator's merge bypasses the two checks below, because enforce_admins is off, and the criterion requires every change to be blocked on a violation. Any such entry fails the check, and so does an OSV that cannot be reached. The audit's only exemption is a .github/vex.toml entry, reviewed like any other change. The required Dependency review check also blocks a change that adds a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or a known licence outside the allow-list, apart from the packages dependency-review.yml exempts by name; a dependency with no detected licence is reported but does not fail. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_06_01_justification: The standard's section 5 sets a threshold of zero for ruff: select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same, in the required lint check. CodeQL runs on every pull request that is not a draft, but the standard sets no threshold for its alerts. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff
osps_vm_06_02_justification: An administrator's merge bypasses the check below, because enforce_admins is off, and the criterion requires every change to be blocked on a violation. The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request that is not a draft (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request that is not a draft but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip32-descriptors/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: REVIEWING.md asks of every change whether what it adds is tested, and the 100% line and branch coverage gate fails a fix whose new code no test runs.
